newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India issues tender to buy November diesel.
newsitem.headline: India issues tender to buy November diesel.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has issued tenders to buy high speed diesel for arrival in November, traders said on Thursday.
The tenders seek both 1.0 and 0.5 percent sulphur diesel.

Cargoes for delivery to Madras or Haldia on the Indian east coast are 45,000 tonnes each, cargoes to Goa and Kandla on the west coast are 30,000 tonnes each, while cargoes to a one-port discharge to Kandla are 45,000 tonnes each.
The tender closes on October 19 and offers will be valid until October 20, traders said.
In its last tender for October delivery, IOC bought a record low of 120,000 tonnes. IOC had also bought unusually low amounts of diesel in September amounting to 255,000 tonnes.
IOC had bought much larger volumes earlier in the year, with August purchases of 800,000 tonnes, 585,000 tonnes in July, 1.5 million tonnes in June and 600,000 tonnes in May.
Traders said the large purchases by IOC earlier in the year had led to a large demurrage bill which forced the company to buy less in September and October in order to clear the port congestion.
